A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research on spatial indexing and visual binding in VLMs. Their complete main texts, figures, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original representational, causal-mediation, attention and intervention experiments on Qwen2-VL-7B, including binding-error recovery and appendix analyses of object ordering.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments across multiple VLMs, including synthetic and naturalistic scenes, COCO interventions, spatial reasoning, counting and binding-error recovery.

M1.justification: The underlying three-stage mechanism is retained: v1's semantic matching heads in Appendix C correspond to v2's ID retrieval heads. Within the existing activation-intervention framework, v2 adds scaled head-output/query edits, cross-task ID injection and COCO prototypes estimated using model-generated object order, extending v1's key/value swaps and residual-stream replacement.

E1.justification: v2 expands beyond colored-shape scenes and color retrieval to PUG photorealistic animal scenes, COCO real-world images, spatial-relation questions and counting tasks involving three to eight objects. These introduce substantive changes in image domains and task requirements, rather than merely additional scores on existing tasks.

E2.justification: v2 introduces bottom-K head ablation as an explicit comparator to top-K ablation on the counting task (Appendix C, Figure 46). v1's all-layer and early-layer key-swap comparison variants are no longer reported. The additional VLM families mainly expand the systems studied, rather than introduce competing algorithms.

E3.justification: The Qwen2-VL-7B-only evaluation expands to multiple Qwen and LLaVA families and sizes, with additional Idefics2 RSA results. Color-retrieval interventions now use alpha=2 and layers containing the top-20 feature-retrieval heads instead of fixed layer ranges. Binding-error recovery changes from replacing the layer-18 residual stream to replacing selected heads' outputs. New experiments also introduce parameter sweeps and separate COCO source/target sets.

E4.justification: v2 adds relative-versus-absolute-position tests, intervention-strength/head-count sensitivity sweeps, cross-task transfer tests and counting ablations. Conversely, v1's detailed attention-profile analyses, raster-order experiments, 4x4 binding-error analyses and key-swap layer-range comparisons are removed rather than merely relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly specifies three random source/target splits for the COCO experiment; this does not establish increased repetitions for retained experiments. v1's recovery table reports accuracies with plus/minus uncertainty values, whereas its replacement in v2 gives only point accuracies.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for naturalistic images, relative coding, spatial reasoning and counting. The recovery table is replaced: v1 reports Qwen2-VL 3x3 accuracy increasing from 89% to 94% under residual patching; v2 reports, for example, Qwen2.5-VL-3B increasing from 69.0% to 80.1% under head patching. These are different experiments, not same-setting gains between versions. Earlier raster-order results are removed.

T1.justification: The CMA score and position/feature RSA definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Sections 4.2–4.4 extend the formal intervention definitions to scaled head-level edits and additive injection of scene-description-derived ID prototypes into spatial reasoning, beyond v1's pairwise key-swap equations. No new theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: v2 adds central claims that position IDs use relative spatial coding, generalize to naturalistic images and are reused across tasks, alongside consistency across model families and scales. The unified three-stage presentation incorporates a retrieval stage already established in v1's appendix; that stage alone is not a new contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of relative coding, qualifies its weaker expression in LLaVA, and discusses possible positional-embedding or training explanations. It also relates recovery efficacy to source-prototype quality and introduces open questions about architectural versus training-driven emergence. v1's specific raster-order interpretation and single-model generality limitation are no longer presented.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands technical documentation with PUG's 200-image generation setup, COCO filtering and prototype-estimation procedures, counting/spatial prompts, and intervention strengths, head selection and parameter sweeps. The original 4x4 generation recipe disappears. A new reproducibility statement promises dataset and code release, but provides no release link.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for PUG, COCO and Griffiths et al., while dropping several architecture/pretraining references, including Löwe, Covert and Tschannen. Related Work adds an explicit distinction from Yang et al.'s text-only circuits based on computational function, distributed visual representations and practical relevance. The overall research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes and rewrites the narrative: Related Work moves earlier, task and architecture explanations receive dedicated subsections, mechanism identification is separated from property-testing results, and contribution and reproducibility statements are added. The conclusion is rewritten, and attention-head terminology is standardized across the main text.

P2.justification: v2 rebuilds Figure 1 as a combined architecture/PCA/RSA/CMA overview, redraws and relocates CMA schematics, and adds extensive model-comparison charts, position-coding illustrations, parameter-sweep panels and COCO/counting figures. Earlier attention maps and raster-order displays disappear, while the recovery table changes structure from grid-based to model-based rows.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's explicit single-model generality limitation through tests across model families and scales, and examines the mechanism in photorealistic and real images and additional reasoning tasks. New causal comparisons and sensitivity analyses strengthen the evidence beyond simple grid scenes. Losing earlier attention/raster-order analyses and recovery-table uncertainties is a drawback, but the stronger support for the mechanism's generality constitutes a substantial net improvement.
